verses.zh: （安息日的诗歌。）称谢耶和华！歌颂你至高者的名！
verses.en: A psalm; a song for the Sabbath day.It is fitting[NOTE:1] to thank the Lord,and to sing praises to your name, O Most High.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 92. The psalmist praises God because he defeats the wicked and vindicates his loyal followers.

verses.zh: 用十弦的乐器和瑟，用琴弹幽雅的声音，早晨传扬你的慈爱；每夜传扬你的信实。这本为美事。
verses.en: It is fitting[NOTE:1] to proclaim your loyal love in the morningand your faithfulness during the night,
notes: The divine title “Most High” (עֶלְיוֹן ʿelyon) pictures God as the exalted ruler of the universe who vindicates the innocent and judges the wicked. See especially Pss 7:17; 9:2; 18:13; 21:7; 47:2.

verses.en: to the accompaniment of a ten-stringed instrument and a lyre,to the accompaniment of the meditative tone of the harp.

verses.zh: 因你―耶和华藉着你的作为叫我高兴，我要因你手的工作欢呼。
verses.en: For you, O Lord, have made me happy by your work.I will sing for joy because of what you have done.[NOTE:1]
notes: The words “it is fitting” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons. Verses 1-3 are actually one long sentence in the Hebrew text, but this has been divided up into two shorter sentences in the translation in keeping with contemporary English style.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你的工作何其大！你的心思极其深！
verses.en: How great are your works, O Lord!Your plans are very intricate![NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 畜类人不晓得；愚顽人也不明白。
verses.en: The spiritually insensitive do not recognize this;the fool does not understand this.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “very deep [are] your thoughts.” God’s “thoughts” refer here to his moral design of the world, as outlined in vv. 6-15.

verses.zh: 恶人茂盛如草，一切作孽之人发旺的时候，正是他们要灭亡，直到永远。
verses.en: When the wicked sprout up like grass,and all the evildoers glisten,[NOTE:1] it is so that they may be annihilated.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the brutish man does not know, and the fool does not understand this.” The adjective בַּעַר (baʿar, “brutish”) refers to spiritual insensitivity, not mere lack of intelligence or reasoning ability (see Pss 49:10; 73:22; Prov 12:1; 30:2, as well as the use of the related verb in Ps 94:8).

verses.zh: 惟你―耶和华是至高，直到永远。
verses.en: But you, O Lord, reign[NOTE:1] forever.
notes: Heb “in order that they might be destroyed permanently.”sn God allows the wicked to prosper temporarily so that he might reveal his justice. When the wicked are annihilated, God demonstrates that wickedness does not pay off.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你的仇敌都要灭亡；一切作孽的也要离散。
verses.en: Indeed,[NOTE:1] look at your enemies, O Lord.Indeed,[NOTE:2] look at how your enemies perish.All the evildoers are scattered.

verses.zh: 你却高举了我的角，如野牛的角；我是被新油膏了的。
verses.en: You exalt my horn like that of a wild ox.[NOTE:1] I am covered[NOTE:2] with fresh oil.
notes: The horn of the wild ox is frequently a metaphor for military strength; the idiom “to exalt/lift up the horn” signifies military victory (see 1 Sam 2:10; Pss 75:10; 89:24; Lam 2:17).

verses.zh: 我眼睛看见仇敌遭报；我耳朵听见那些起来攻击我的恶人受罚。
verses.en: I gloat in triumph over those who tried to ambush me;[NOTE:1] I hear the defeated cries of the evil foes who attacked me.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew verb בָּלַל (balal) usually has the nuance “to mix.” Here it seems to mean “to smear” or “to anoint.” Some emend the form to בַּלֹּתַנִי (ballotani; a second person form of the verb with a first person suffix) and read, “you anoint me.”

Heb “my eye gazes upon my walls.” See also Pss 5:8; 27:11; 56:2. The form שׁוּרָי shuray, “my walls”) should be emended to שׁוֹרְרָי (shoreray, “my foes” or perhaps “those who rebel against me” or “those who malign me”). See HALOT 1454 s.v. שׁוֹרֵר and also Pss 5:8; 27:11; 56:2.

verses.zh: 义人要发旺如棕树，生长如黎巴嫩的香柏树。
verses.en: The godly[NOTE:1] grow like a palm tree;they grow high like a cedar in Lebanon.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “those who rise up against me, evil [foes], my ears hear.”
The singular is used in a representative sense, with the typical godly person being in view.

verses.zh: 他们栽于耶和华的殿中，发旺在我们　神的院里。
verses.en: Planted in the Lord’s house,they grow in the courts of our God.

verses.zh: 他们年老的时候仍要结果子，要满了汁浆而常发青，
verses.en: They bear fruit even when they are old;they are filled with vitality and have many leaves.[NOTE:1]
notes: The cedars of the Lebanon forest were well-known in ancient Israel for their immense size.

verses.zh: 好显明耶和华是正直的。他是我的磐石，在他毫无不义。
verses.en: So they proclaim that the Lord, my Protector,is just and never unfair.[NOTE:1]
